metadata.case_name: CHU KA WAI v. HOP HING FURNITURE CO LTD AND ANOTHER

source: X-ray of his right elbow revealed right olecranon fracture.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of upper end of ulna

injuries.description: acute right epidural haemorrhage with compression and effacement of ipsilateral lateral and third ventricles, and midline shift to the left
source: Computed tomography of his brain showed acute right epidural haemorrhage with compression and effacement of ipsilateral lateral and third ventricles, and midline shift to the left.
He also suffered right temporal bone fracture.
injuries.icd_description: Other fractures of base of skull

source: Medical examination by the Department of Accident and Emergency showed that he had suffered loss of consciousness and seizure for one minute.
injuries.icd_description: Concussion with loss of consciousness, short duration of less than 30 minutes

manifestations.description: residual pain, stiffness and weakness over his right elbow
dizziness aggravated by big movement especially extension and weather changes
difficulty in concentration on and performance of certain mental tasks
loss of consciousness and seizure for one minute

source: Mr Chu was admitted to Tuen Mun Hospital immediately after the accident.

treatments_received.treatment: treatment from the Department of Neurosurgery
source: He received treatment from the Department of Neurosurgery and the Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology.

treatments_received.treatment: treatment from the Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology
source: He received treatment from the Department of Neurosurgery and the Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology.
He further received treatment from the Physiotherapy Department and completed 22 sessions of out-patient physiotherapy in Tuen Mun Hospital.
Lastly, Mr Chu also received occupational therapy treatment.

treatments_future.treatment: clinic visits for headaches and dizziness (4 visits annually)
source: Mr Chu probably needs 4 visits to the clinic annually and each visit would cost him HK$400.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Mr Chu claims to be unable to pursue his pre-accident hobbies including boxing, basketball and snooker due to his residual pain.
He has occasional headaches and difficulty in concentration on and performance of certain mental tasks. He alleges memory impairment, insomnia and irritability.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Before the accident he was responsible for all the repair and handyman jobs at home. However, after the accident, given his medical condition, he has difficulty in performing such works for his family.
